checks: The physical martingale and affineness of q make ∫q dP=q_s>0. The L tilt is normalized by V_s>0. Both densities relative to P are positive and their ratio is q(t)V_s/(q_s L(t)).

Multiplying its logarithm integrated under Q_s by q_s gives ∫F_q dP + q_s log(V_s/q_s), and subtracting the source F_q gives precisely q_s[log(L(s)/V_s)+D(Q_s||T_s)]. Concavity of L gives V_s≤L(s) and the entropy is nonnegative.

The supremum in the proof is attained at 1+log(q/L). Each term in the supremum is convex because q is affine and the coefficient of concave L is negative. Applying Jensen first to the source-to-midpoint martingale and then to each pair gives ∫F_q dν≤∫F_q dρ≤∫F_q dη. Applying affineness twice gives equality of the q masses.

Compactness and continuity bound the row integrands. Zero total flow gives zero for all integrated assertions. The source §10 uses the same normalization. Its extra discounted-repair application is outside this candidate's scope.

overlap.comparison: Its logarithmic surface reserve corresponds to a constant q in the sign comparison. It does not give the two normalized tilted probability laws for a positive variable affine q or their exact row identity.
The accepted relative entropy is for a volume law obtained by L-tilting an inverse-volume row. Here both tilts are on the same physical surface probability row, and their ratio compares q to L.

readability: The normal mark stays with the physical row. It is not an argument of q or L. The entropy orientation is Q_s relative to T_s.

summary: The two tilted laws give the exact row identity, and two Jensen applications give the claimed reserve and fixed affine mass.
